5. After considering the pleadings of the parties, evidence and other materials on record, the trial Court was pleased lo decree the suit holding, infer alia, that the plaintiff managed to prove his lawful right, title, interest and possession in, and dispossession from, the suit land by adducing oral and documentary evidence; that the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiff on the strength of his pattan from the erstwhile Zaminder, and that admitting his title to the suit land, the then East Pakistan Government gave the plaintiff compensation following the requisition of the same. 

 6. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, the defendants as appellants tiled Title Appeal No. 46 of 1984 before the learned District Judge, Bogra and on transferred the same was heard by the then learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Bogra and after hearing, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was pleased to allow the appeal holding, inter alia, that the plaintiff failed to mention the date of his pattan from the Zaminder in the plaint and he did not take any step to prove his documents formally in support of his claim by calling for the register from the concerned land acquisition office to proves compensation against requisition and, as such, the plaintiff failed to proves his title to the suit land. 

 8. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan with Mr. SM Abul Kalam Azad (appearing in person), the learned advocates for the plaintiff-petitioners submit that the predecessor of the petitioners took settlement of the suit land from the then Zaminder Maharaja Birendra Nath Roy Chowdhury on 7th Chaitra, 1354 BS upon payment of appropriate salami and paid the rent to the said Zaminder, and to the Government after the acquisition of the rent receiving interest of the suit land by the Government, and on 31-12-1952 the suit land as appearing in Schedule Kha was requisitioned by the Government and on 20-10-1958 the same was derequisitioned in his favour and on 23-11-1958 the vacant possession thereof was handed over to him and since then he had been enjoying and possessing the same openly, adversely, exclusively and peacefully to the knowledge of all concerned including the defendants till his dispossession there from in the first part of February, 1966. He also submits the plaintiff managed to proves his lawful right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the strength of settlement dated 7th Chaitra, 1354 BS from the then Zaminder Maharaja Birendra Nath Roy Chowdhury and he also managed to proves unlawful dispossession from Schedule 'Ka' land and threat to be disposed from Schedule Kha land which was supported by the PWs. On placing the deposition of the DWs, Mr. Bhuiyan submits that the defendants miserably failed to proves their allotment in the suit land by the Government by adducing any minimum iota of evidence, either oral or documentary, The learned Advocate for the petitioners next submits that the mere omission of the trial Court or its officers/staffs to sign and seal the pattannama, salami receipt, rent receipts and other documents submitted by plaintiff in support of his title to and possession in the suit land does not affect the merit of the suit and such omissions being mere defects or irregularities in the procedure within the meaning of section 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court of appeal below ought to have cured those defects or irregularities in exercise of its inherent power under section 151 of the said Code and having not been done, the impugned judgment and decree is illegal and liable to be set aside. He also submits that the learned Judge of the Court of appeal below committed a serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in misreading and non-reading the plaint and recording a patently perverse finding that the plaintiff did not mention the date of his pattan in the plaint. Mr. Bhuiyan also submits that the court of appeal below failed to take into consideration that the plaintiff filed information slip to show the receipt of compensation money and also filed an application before both the courts below to call for the records from the land acquisition office, but the said court committed a gross illegality in holding that the plaintiff did not take any step to call for the records of the LA Case.
